The framework can be extended to additional source-target GSD combinations by incorporating corresponding image pairs into training. On the 20-to-10 m pair, the model achieved competitive perceptual performance compared with pair-specific baselines, with LPIPS of 0.2236, DISTS of 0.2431, and NIQE of 8.9020. Experiments using the same architecture demonstrated the value of acquiring real-world multi-altitude UAV image pairs for SR training, with real-pair training achieving better average reconstruction performance across the 21 altitude pairs than training with the tested synthetic degradation pipeline. Downstream zero-shot segmentation case studies illustrated task-dependent benefits of super-resolved imagery for crop monitoring, suggesting potential UAV flight-time savings through image acquisition at higher altitudes.

new ReTrace: Visual Backtracking for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

Authors: Guangzong Si, Dong Wang, Yifan Yu, Miao Liu, Panwang Pan, Wentao Zhu

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) encode images into dense visual token sequences, creating substantial attention and KV-cache overhead. Existing visual token compression methods reduce this cost by pruning low-saliency tokens in shallow layers, but this practice couples temporary computational deactivation with irreversible information deletion. We show that this coupling breaks an intrinsic inference pattern in MLLMs. Through layer-wise attention analysis, we identify \textbf{Visual Backtracking}: visual pivots remain spatially stable, yet in middle layers they actively retrieve context from tokens that appeared unimportant earlier. Thus, early low-saliency tokens can be inactive for computation while still being useful for later reasoning. Motivated by this finding, we propose \textbf{ReTrace}, a backtracking-aware compression framework that introduces a dormant token state. ReTrace caches non-pivot tokens outside expensive layer-wise computation, restores them during the backtracking window, and prunes only after their information has been absorbed. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 demonstrate nearly 90\% reductions in FLOPs and KV cache, a 2.83$\times$ prefilling speedup, and strong performance retention across complex vision-language benchmarks.

new FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats

Authors: Hyebin Kim, Hwasik Jeong, Joonhyuk Park, Gyeongjin Kang, Jungwoo Kim, Younghyun Kim, Eunbyung Park

Abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) promises instant scene reconstruction with high-quality novel-view synthesis. Yet, fine-grained geometry and appearance remain difficult to recover, motivating us to revisit how feed-forward models represent, aggregate, and refine detailed visual information. We introduce FineSplat, a feed-forward 3DGS framework built around fine-grained image patches. Since global multi-view attention becomes prohibitively expensive at such high token resolutions, we develop a dual-grouping strategy that combines two complementary forms of locality: view-wise grouping enables efficient interaction among neighboring views, while 3D spatial grouping reconnects geometrically related tokens that may never have interacted under view-wise grouping by lifting them into the 3D scene space. We further leverage reconstruction error as direct feedback, providing an explicit rendering-based signal to recover fine-grained structures and appearance, thereby overcoming the limitations of one-pass feed-forward prediction. Finally, a compact Gaussian generation scheme preserves the benefits of fine-grained features without unnecessarily increasing the number of primitives. Together, these designs enable FineSplat to recover richer geometry and appearance while remaining efficient and compact, achieving state-of-the-art results by a substantial margin, under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets than existing methods.

new IECLA: Interpretable Emotion Contribution Learning for Affective Image Editing

Authors: Yijie Guo, Dexiang Hong, Weidong Chen, Xinyan Liu, Zhendong Mao

Abstract: Affective image editing (AIE) aims to evoke a target emotion while preserving the content and structure of a source image. Existing methods improve emotional expression or visual fidelity, but the target emotion alone does not reveal which source regions should be changed and which should remain intact, especially in complex scenes. IECLA constructs signed object-level supervision through counterfactual interventions and trains a context-conditioned contribution predictor to localize evidence that supports or opposes the source emotion. At inference, an image-level evaluator estimates the source emotion directly from the input, while the predictor identifies editable and preservation evidence without repeated interventions. Extensive evaluations show that IECLA predicts counterfactual contributions more faithfully on both in-domain and cross-dataset tests, while external VLM and independent human references support the quality of its localized evidence. Across six editing backbones, IECLA consistently strengthens target-emotion expression while preserving image content and structure, and user studies further show improved perceived target expression and naturalness.

new PRET is a few-shot system for pan-cancer recognition without example training

Authors: Yi Li, Ziyu Ning, Tianqi Xiang, Qixiang Zhang, Zhihao Lin, Min Yi, Feiyan Feng, Baozhen Zeng, Xuexia Qian, Lu Sun, Jiace Qin, Ling Xiang, Chao Fan, Tian Qin, Qian Wang, Xiu-Wu Bian, Kun-Hsing Yu, Kang Zhang, Qingling Zhang, Xiaomeng Li

Abstract: Pathological examination stands as the cornerstone in cancer diagnosis, impacting millions worldwide annually. With the shortage of pathologists globally, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged rapidly to automate the diagnostics process. However, conventional AI models require substantial labeled data for each disease, posing huge challenges in scalability and practicality. Therefore, we introduce PRET (pan-cancer recognition without examples training), a few-shot system to achieve flexible, scalable, and effective cancer recognition across diverse organs, hospitals and tasks without training. Evaluated on 23 international benchmarks comprising 4,484 whole-slide images, our method outperforms existing approaches across 20 tasks, achieving over 97% area under the curve on 15 benchmarks with a maximum improvement of 36.76%. Notably, PRET delivers clinical-grade diagnostic performance in lymph node metastasis detection using only eight slide examples, outperforming 11 pathologists. By offering a flexible and cost-effective solution for pan-cancer recognition, PRET paves the way for accessible and equitable AI-based pathology systems, particularly benefiting minority populations and underserved regions.

new MoWE: Spatially Adaptive Mixture-of-Wavelet-Experts Pooling for Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation

Authors: Reaz Hassan Joarder, Sidratul Tanzila Tasmi, Alif Arshad Bakshi, Md. Bakhtiar Hasan, Md Hasanul Kabir

Abstract: We present Mixture-of-Wavelet-Experts (MoWE), a spatially adaptive routing mechanism that replaces max-pooling and strided convolutions in U-Net architectures for ultrasound lesion segmentation. Standard pooling operations suppress high-frequency spatial details, including potential boundary cues in speckled regions. Recent frequency-domain methods preserve some of these details, but a single wavelet family applies the same spectral bias across the image. MoWE instead uses a context-aware router to assign local regions to fixed wavelet families according to local texture and global feature context. The decoder reuses the encoder's spatial routing maps during the inverse transform. Learnable channel-wise gates rescale the high-frequency subbands before reconstruction. We evaluate MoWE with U-Net on four ultrasound lesion benchmarks (BUSI, TN3K, UDIAT, BUS-UCLM) and one cardiac dataset (CAMUS), and with nnU-Net on BUSI. On BUSI, MoWE improves U-Net Dice from 72.59\% to 74.55\% and reduces HD95 from 47.01 to 43.49\,px. With nnU-Net, MoWE improves Dice from 80.18\% to 81.97\% and reduces ASSD from 20.07 to 17.25\,px. On U-Net, MoWE reduces trainable parameters by 6.4\%.

new MoCKEFA: Model-Conditioned Keyframe Extraction and Fair Attribution for Video Model Explanation

Authors: Lahiru Wijayasingha

Abstract: We show that a video can be represented with just a few keyframes without sacrificing a given model's belief about the video. Our method is the first of its kind that extracts these keyframes conditioned on the model's prediction, which is massively helpful for building explainable video models. We then fairly distribute the importance of the video to the model among the keyframes with game theoretically fair Shapley values. Through qualitative and quantitative experiments, we show that keyframe attribution is superior to the traditional frame attribution. Further, we conduct preliminary exploration on highlighting the important changes among the frames by looking at the differences between adjacent keyframes.

new Sufficient Frame Subsets for Video Understanding

Authors: Lahiru Wijayasingha

Abstract: Understanding when during a video a model makes its critical observations is essential for interpreting video-understanding systems. However, existing attribution methods often spread evidence diffusely across near-duplicate frames. We introduce Sufficient Frame Subsets: compact sets of frames in which all other frames are masked, yet each subset independently preserves the model's prediction. We evaluate our method on two complementary benchmarks, UCF101 and Something-Something v2, using both CNN- and transformer-based architectures. Our results show that the proposed algorithm identifies highly compact and effective frame subsets for explaining model decisions. We also find that models capable of relying on a greater number of sufficient frame subsets tend to perform better, possibly because they are more robust, consistent with prior research. Finally, the extracted frame subsets help us analyze model failure cases, reveal which aspects of a video the model has learned to emphasize, and identify opportunities for improving future training procedures.

new Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation

Authors: Junwei Wen, Deshui Miao, Guangming Lu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Xin Li, Wenjie Pei

Abstract: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) requires a model to identify an implicitly described target and predict its pixel-level mask trajectory, while resolving the spatial relations and temporal events that determine the answer. Text-only Chain-of-Thought (CoT) can explain a target choice without making the underlying visual references explicit, leaving a \emph{video reference gap} between linguistic inference and the evidence distributed across frames. We introduce \textbf{Temporal Chain of Video Primitives (TCoVP)}, a spatiotemporally grounded form of Video CoT that organizes query-relevant observations into a chronological reasoning chain. Each primitive associates an entity reference with temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence, and the chain interleaves these references with language to guide reasoning about which entity is relevant, when the queried event holds, and where its evidence appears. The selected target primitives then provide box prompts and temporal support for video mask prediction. We construct TCoVP-SFT-15k and TCoVP-RL-13k to learn this representation through supervised fine-tuning and chain-aligned reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones demonstrate the strong performance of TCoVP, highlighting the effectiveness of organizing spatial and temporal evidence within the reasoning process. All models and code will be publicly released. Project page: \url{https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/}

URLs: https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/

new LC-TSRNet: A Land-Cover-Guided Two-Stage Network for Annual MODIS Surface Reflectance Time Series Reconstruction

Authors: Wenjuan Zhang, Xuesong Ma, Zhen Li, Meixiang Wang, Caimeng Yi, Jie Pan, Nan Su, Bing Zhang

Abstract: MODIS surface reflectance (SR) products often suffer from data gaps due to cloud contamination and sensor malfunctions, limiting their applications in long-term and large-scale studies. Most existing methods rely on cloud-free observations from optical time series or introduce SAR time series as auxiliary information. However, due to the coarse spatial resolution of MODIS, cloud-free reference images are difficult to obtain, and SAR imagery is not well matched to the spatial resolution of MODIS, making it difficult to provide effective prior constraints. To address these issues, this study proposes LC-TSRNet for seamless reconstruction of annual MODIS SR products. In the first stage, an annual land cover map is introduced as prior knowledge, and CSPM is designed by leveraging the spectral similarity within identical land cover types, thereby providing prior spectral constraints for missing regions. In the second stage, to address large-area, persistent, and overlapping gaps in MODIS imagery, SMRM is designed to adaptively exploit and integrate multi-scale spatiotemporal contextual information. Meanwhile, to address the limited collaborative utilization of spatio-temporal-spectral information, 3DAM is designed to impose cross-dimensional joint constraints. Considering the lack of publicly available MODIS sample datasets, this study constructs the AIRMOD-TSR dataset. Extensive experimental results show that LC-TSRNet outperforms the comparison methods and achieves better reconstruction accuracy and spectral fidelity. Under the spatially adjacent scenario, LC-TSRNet improves PSNR by 0.56 dB and reduces SAM by 0.13{\deg}. The vegetation monitoring application further verifies the practical value of the reconstructed SR time series.

Authors: Faisal Mohammad, Mohamed Younis

Abstract: Recognizing a vessel's type from an image supports maritime surveillance and sanctions monitoring, but a classifier can reach high accuracy by leaning on the generic hull instead of the more distinctive superstructure, and is then fooled when a vessel is re-hulled or occluded. De-biasing methods claim to remove such reliance, yet the field certifies them with worst-group accuracy, a proxy that needs group labels and only infers reliance from accuracy. We measure the reliance directly. HullProbe swaps a registered anatomical part of a vessel for another instance's and reads how much that part drives the decision, using a same-class swap to control for compositing artifacts. Because a surface vessel is a hull and a superstructure arranged along one axis, its parts form a 2x3 grid whose 2^6 = 64 swaps we evaluate exhaustively, and a single Walsh transform returns each part's interventional influence and its interaction spectrum. On planted shortcuts, where the true reliance is known, the measure tracks worst-group accuracy (r = -0.94 over 45 configurations), and replacing its learned segmenter with human annotations changes the hull-share by less than the audit's resolution. On the 26 vessel types of MARVEL, the classifier places about 46% of its corrected sensitivity on the generic hull yet follows the superstructure when the two conflict, and the group-label-free de-biasers available there do not detectably reduce the hull's share. The findings hold across three architectures and a second maritime dataset, and the method extends to fine-grained vehicle recognition on Stanford Cars.

Authors: Shuo Xu, Hanrui Ying, Debin Liu, Jianjun Li, Zhiyuan Ma

Abstract: Fine-grained rectification of existing generations under a limited additional budget remains a key problem in test-time optimization (TTO) for image generation. As for prior approaches, they could identify residual errors, but could not directly ensure that the model acts on the feedback during reasoning. Such errors stem from multiple sources, such as the initial noise or text prompt, and ultimately induce an execution gap of failing to handle potential deviations along the trajectory generating. However, classic models generally cannot remedy this gap. To narrow it, we propose Reflection-Guided Dynamics Rectification (RGDR), which turns reflections on completed outputs into corrective interventions on the process of sampling dynamics at the trajectory level. Specifically, RGDR could impact every sampling step by adapting to instantaneous intervention. Moreover, RGDR generates flexible candidates while adjudicating between them and the reference. As experiments show, rectification from RGDR starts from the existing base trajectory and reflection, and RGDR is substantially more effective than former trajectory exploration. Under matched budgets for additional image generation, RGDR's gain in the cross-model average final checklist score over the reference is $1.51\times$ that of TIR prompt refinement and $1.81\times$ that of Dynamic CFG.

Authors: Le-Anh Tran

Abstract: Image dehazing is traditionally addressed through handcrafted physical priors or task-specific deep learning models, often requiring carefully designed architectures or extensive model training. Authors: Jianghao Yin, Lang Yu, Qianxi Yu, Qin Chen, Jie Zhou, Zhikai Lei, Liang He

The results show that our method effectively reduces hallucinations across models of different types and sizes while introducing minimal inference latency. Compared to advanced baselines, our model also demonstrates superior performance.

Authors: Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Zhen Xing, Bojia Zi, Xiaoling Wang

Abstract: Controllable video generation has recently achieved impressive visual quality, yet existing control paradigms remain poorly suited to embodied navigation. new Evaluating Cloud and Self-Hosted OCR Systems for Arabic, English, and French Documents: Bounding Box Detection, Text Recognition, and Mathematical Expression Recognition

Authors: Jumana Alsubhi, Ahmed Alhusayni, Abdulrahman Gharawi, Israa Hamdine, Khadija Alansari, Alshaymaa Allahim, Lamees Alhumaid, Ahmad Shabana

Abstract: Choosing an OCR system for a multilingual archive requires balancing accuracy against deployment constraints. Authors: Yuchen Xi, Yuhan Guo, Chenwei Hou, Zixu Liu, Jin Fang, Jason Liu, Ruigang Yang

Project page: https://xiyuche.github.io/GeoV2V/

URLs: https://xiyuche.github.io/GeoV2V/

new Visual Scaffolding: Toward Native Multimodal Reasoning

Authors: Run Shao, Zhaoyang Zhang, Ziyu Li, Linrui Xu, Ji Qi, Xiu Su, Yichao Cao, Chao Tao, Haifeng Li

Abstract: The success of chain-of-thought (CoT) in complex reasoning can be attributed to a textual scaffolding effect: explicit intermediate results can be examined, reused, and composed to support subsequent reasoning, much as scaffolding supports a building under construction. However, mainstream multimodal LLMs lack an equivalent scaffold for visual distinctions that are difficult to express in concise verbal descriptions. We therefore ask: Can native visual representations become first-class citizens alongside language, providing a visual scaffold for reasoning? We define native multimodal reasoning as reasoning in which native visual representations and language jointly carry reusable intermediate states. As a concrete implementation, the visual scaffolding mechanism we proposed lets the MLLM autonomously initiate a retrieval action at any reasoning step. A lightweight retriever selects native visual features, which are then incorporated directly into the evolving CoT and remain available to subsequent steps. To evaluate this mechanism under controlled visual demands, we introduce NMR-Bench, comprising Burden Counting and Path Tracing. With 88M added parameters (approximately 2%) on Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking, our model achieves 66.43% and 72.50% accuracy, respectively, surpassing the evaluated GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro baselines. Controlled interventions show that changing selected visual content affects task accuracy and can redirect subsequent visual selection even when intervening text is held fixed. These findings show that native visual states can function as intermediate reasoning material and point toward reusable scaffolds for additional modalities.

new Persistent Representational Misalignment Induces Vision-Language Model Failures

Authors: Yonatan Gideoni, Yoav Gelberg, Tim G. J. Rudner, Yarin Gal

Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) fail at some tasks that are simple for humans---but why? We hypothesize that many such failures stem from VLMs' difficulties translating between vision and language representations, a misalignment the Platonic Representation Hypothesis predicts should disappear with scale. This paper is composed of two parts: in the first, we show that existing vision and language representations are linearly unalignable. This misalignment is an inherent property of the data and hence expected to persist regardless of either scale or the alignment's complexity. In the second, we demonstrate how this misalignment both leads to a predictably induced generalization failure and correlates with existing failure modes, where more representationally aligned VLM backbones accordingly exhibit fewer failures. Overall, these results imply representations will not become aligned simply given sufficient scale, providing evidence against a strong version of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

new PanoDent-KD: From Generalist Knowledge Distillation to Cross-Dataset Specialist Detection and Embedded Deployment in Panoramic Radiographs

Authors: Muhammad Waqas Ashraf, Imad Ali Shah, Ali Hassan

Abstract: Reliable panoramic-radiograph detection requires consistency across datasets with different class definitions and deployment software. We present PanoDent-KD, an auditable 1280-pixel YOLO26m pipeline linking a 12-class source generalist, feature-level knowledge distillation (KD), exact classifier-row transfer, teacher-free five-class specialization, and embedded deployment. A common training and evaluation pipeline compares three source-training arms across three seeds: a supervised baseline (B1), single-teacher KD (STKD), and multi-teacher KD (MTKD). Five shared classifier rows initialize nine OralXrays-9 specialists, while the backbone, FPN-PAN neck, and dual-detection-head topology are retained unchanged. On the 2,686-image test subset, all three arms achieve macro box F1 near 0.82. B1 achieves the highest three-seed arm-level mean macro box F1 (0.8239$\pm$0.0027) and $mAP_{50:95}$ (0.6130$\pm$0.0067). STKD seed 1, selected after development but before final testing, was used for deployment. Its Jetson Orin Nano Super FP16 TensorRT engine achieves 77.03-ms median and 80.86-ms P95 prediction-call latency, throughput of 12.90 images/s, and gross total-module energy of 1.39 J/image, with high numerical agreement between within-device PyTorch and TensorRT FP16 inference. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of an auditable, device-specific deployment workflow, but do not establish clinical validity or improved target-domain accuracy from KD.

new GeoART: Geometry-Aware Refinement via Test-Time Scaling for Camera-Conditioned Video Diffusion

Authors: Liudi Yang, Ziyuan Liu

Abstract: Camera-conditioned video diffusion models often suffer from inaccurate camera control and geometric inconsisten- cies because camera constraints and estimated geometry are only weakly enforced during denoising. Existing reme- dies often require costly geometry-aware fine-tuning or ad- ditional 3D supervision. We introduce GeoART, a training- free self-refinement framework that improves camera con- trollability through geometry-aware test-time scaling. At selected denoising steps, GeoART generates multiple can- didates within the Predict-and-Perturb cycle and eval- uates them using a geometry prior, without directly modify- ing the denoising trajectory. A confidence gate suppresses unreliable geometric evidence, while rank-calibrated prob- abilistic selection combines score magnitude and relative rank to choose the next refinement state. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in camera controlla- bility, multi-view consistency, and visual quality over exist- ing sampling and self-refinement methods, without training or modifying the pretrained video diffusion model

new Holo4D: Holistic 4D Reconstruction as Geometric Control for Video Diffusion

Authors: Yushi Lan, Zeren Jiang, Koichi Namekata, Xingang Pan, Chuanxia Zheng, Andrea Vedaldi

Abstract: Synthesizing a monocular video from a new camera trajectory requires preserving the observed scene geometry and motion while completing regions that become newly visible. Feed-forward 4D reconstructors recover the structure of the observed scene, whereas video diffusion models provide a generative prior for completing unseen content. We introduce Holo4D, a video reshooting framework that uses reconstructed 3D trajectories as a holistic source-view 4D scaffold. We project these trajectories into the requested views and encode their geometry and source appearance to guide a pretrained video diffusion model. Together with the source video and target cameras, the scaffold grounds generation in reconstructed observations while leaving unsupported regions to the generative prior. Experiments demonstrate the value of trajectory-based conditioning for camera control and novel-view synthesis. The framework accommodates different 4D reconstructors without retraining the video generator, allowing it to benefit from future advances in source reconstruction. More details can be found in our project page.

new Learning Lane-Structured Conditioning Fields for Online HD Mapping

Authors: Andrea Bertogalli, Anthony Dell'Eva, Marcello Ceresini, Federico Pirazzoli, Lorenzo Cipelli, Filippo D'Addeo, Nicola Marinello, Massimo Bertozzi

Abstract: High-definition maps provide critical structural information for downstream autonomous driving tasks. Recent methods increasingly rely on external priors to improve prediction accuracy and robustness. Yet, existing prior representations expose a trade-off: dense rasters are easy to integrate but ignore certain map geometric properties, while sparse vectors preserve geometric structure but require dedicated encoders and are difficult to plug into existing architectures. Moreover, external priors can be inaccurate, costly to acquire, or difficult to maintain, motivating a structural representation that can provide geometric guidance while remaining learnable and broadly applicable. We address this limitation with the Lane Field, a dense BEV-aligned geometric representation that encodes local lane structure at each spatial location and can be either predicted from onboard observations or constructed from external map priors. Building on this representation, we introduce a plug-and-play framework that enhances online HD mapping through two complementary mechanisms: BEV feature modulation, which injects lane-structured cues into latent BEV features, and deformable attention guidance, which steers query sampling toward the underlying lane geometry. We primarily evaluate our method on OpenLane-V2, showing that conditioning BEV features and guiding deformable attention with local lane geometry enables our framework to consistently improve existing methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance on lane segment perception. Project page: https://andberto.github.io/LaneField/

URLs: https://andberto.github.io/LaneField/

new The Explainability Illusion: Must ViTs Exhibit Patch-Decoding Interpretability?

Authors: Ronen Schaffer, Hila Manor, Tomer Michaeli

Abstract: Transformers are widely assumed to exhibit token-decoding explainability. In particular, in vision transformer (ViT) classifiers, decoding individual patch tokens has become a common diagnostic tool due to its tendency to yield human-interpretable outputs. In light of the increasing popularity of this approach, an important question is whether token-decoding explainability is an inherent property of transformers that should be expected to hold across architectures, scales, and training objectives, or merely an artifact of some implicit bias. In this paper we systematically study token-decoding explainability across diverse ViT settings, spanning architectures, scales, and training objectives, using both controlled experiments and real-world models. We find that while some models indeed exhibit aligned and interpretable token decodings, others exhibit either inverted explainability maps or a complete lack of correlation with the image semantics. As we show, these tendencies toward different explainability behaviors are not intrinsic to the architecture and can vary arbitrarily with changes in the optimization landscape. We provide theoretical support for these observations by demonstrating a setting where a single fixed toy transformer architecture can provably implement the optimal classification rule in multiple ways, which differ in their patch-decoding explainability patterns. Our results show that token-decoding explainability is not an inherent property of trained transformers, but rather an outcome contingent on the problem setting and thus should not be a-priori assumed to hold. Code can be found in https://ronensc.github.io/Explainability-Illusion/ .

URLs: https://ronensc.github.io/Explainability-Illusion/

new MotionShift: Environment-Compatible Motion Transfer via Planner-Evaluator Synergistic Adaptation

Authors: Yanchen Liu, Junyao Gao, Yanan Sun, Wensheng Chen, Guangming Lu, Wenjie Pei

Abstract: Existing motion transfer methods excel at exact, rigid motion replication from reference videos to target scenes, whereas they often fail to account for the compatibility between the transferred motion and the target scene environment in accordance with physical laws. In this work, we propose MotionShift, a novel motion transfer framework that achieves high-fidelity motion transfer while ensuring physical compatibility with the target scene. In particular, we design a planner--evaluator iterative motion adaptation mechanism, in which a Large Language Model (LLM) acts as the planner to generate motion trajectories by leveraging its strong semantic reasoning capabilities, while a Vision-Language Model (VLM) serves as the evaluator to rectify the motion based on its superior visual perception and scene understanding. Through this planner--evaluator synergistic reasoning process, the motion is adapted to the target scene in a training-free manner. The adapted motion is then used as a generative condition for an image-to-video (I2V) model to render videos in the target scene. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MotionShift achieves high-fidelity and physically compatible motion transfer across diverse and complex scenes. Moreover, we show that MotionShift can be readily integrated into existing trajectory-conditioned I2V models, endowing them with realistic motion transfer capabilities.

new SENRI: Understanding the Space-Event Nexus in Real-Life Videos

Authors: Kehan Lan, Kaining Ying, Henghui Ding, Kaipeng Zhang

Abstract: Human memories are organized in a way that connects events with their corresponding spatial contexts. An AI assistant should also be able to memorize and recall the nexus of events and spaces. Thus we introduce SENRI, a task that studies this space--event connection in long, continuous real-life egocentric video. It contains six task types in two directions: Event$\rightarrow$Space, which recovers spatial knowledge from event cues, and Space$\rightarrow$Event, which retrieves events from regions and trajectories. To evaluate this, we build SENRI-Bench, containing 500 manually annotated multiple-choice questions over 10 uninterrupted self-recorded videos with around 25.3 hours of content. Also, we evaluate three typical long video understanding paradigms: direct perception, evidence seeking, and persistent memory. The task remains challenging across all three paradigms, highlighting substantial room for improvement. Then we show two representative failure modes of existing memory methods and address these evidence gaps with SENRI-Agent, a controller that uses Target-Guided Visual Check (TGVC) to propose local visual check tasks for parallel verifiers and integrate the reports into a working memory to help with reasoning. Built upon existing memory systems, SENRI-Agent improves the performance of existing baselines without modifying their stored memories. We hope SENRI will provide valuable insights into how real-life egocentric understanding should be evaluated, reveal the gaps in existing approaches, and offer a possible direction for improvement.

new MPIG: Multi-angle Polarization Image Generation from a Single Polarization Observation

Authors: Jue Wang, Ruilin Huang, Liquan Shen, Zhen Tian, Xia Hua

Abstract: Polarization imaging provides informative cues for material analysis, scene understanding, and visual perception. However, acquiring complete polarization observations typically requires specialized hardware and multi-angle measurements, thereby increasing system complexity and limiting practical deployment. In this work, we address the problem of predicting the missing $45^\circ$, $90^\circ$, and $135^\circ$ polarization views from a single $0^\circ$ observation by leveraging a learned scene prior. To this end, we propose MPIG (Multi-angle Polarization Image Generation), a Swin Transformer-based framework that couples cross-angle feature interaction with residual decoding to predict angle-dependent intensity variations while preserving shared scene structure. Specifically, measured Stokes differences and polarization-strength-aware supervision guide the recovery of polarization modulation, orientation, and magnitude, while low-rank factorization further reduces the decoding cost. We also construct HighPol, a large-scale real-world polarization dataset comprising 5,474 groups of high-resolution four-angle polarization images collected from diverse indoor and outdoor scenes. Experimental results demonstrate improved image and polarization accuracy, achieving 29.729 dB PSNR, 0.9505 SSIM, and $21.514^\circ$ AoLP MAngE while requiring 85.86 M parameters and 1.126 T FLOPs. Furthermore, downstream validation on glass and semantic-segmentation tasks suggests that the generated polarization images can preserve task-relevant information, demonstrating the effectiveness of MPIG and the practical utility of predicted polarization observations for downstream vision applications.

new CoRe-WM: Conditioned Response-State World Modeling for Longitudinal Treatment-Response Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI

Authors: Lin Zhao, Bowen Chen, Qiaohui Gao, Shaowen Wan, Xiang Li, Wei Liu, Tianming Liu

Abstract: Pathologic complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is a key prognostic indicator in aggressive breast cancer, yet existing prediction approaches either rely on pretreatment imaging alone, missing the patient's evolving response, or optimize multi-visit classifiers under direct outcome supervision, coupling representation learning with the clinical endpoint. We formulate longitudinal pCR prediction as a world-modeling problem and propose Conditioned Response-state World Modeling (CoRe-WM), which learns a latent state-transition model that predicts the next imaging state from the observed sequence. The transition function is conditioned on patient clinical profile and assigned therapy through additive shift and feature-wise modulation, enabling patient- and treatment-specific dynamics. A Factorized Response State pathway further decouples treatment-response dynamics from imaging appearance by encoding the structural prior that response manifests primarily in lesion morphology. After pretraining, all parameters are frozen and a linear readout predicts pCR at each clinical decision point. We evaluate CoRe-WM on I-SPY2 under five-fold cross-validation and assess cross-cohort transfer on I-SPY1. CoRe-WM achieves the highest discrimination among all evaluated methods at every prospective decision point, and demonstrates robust cross-cohort transfer. Ablation studies identify patient-profile conditioning and the factorized response pathway as the principal contributors. These results establish world-model-based representation learning as a promising framework for outcome prediction in oncology and beyond.

new Edge Deployable Lightweight Framework for Real-Time Driver Safety System with Integrated Lane Departure and Traffic Sign Recognition

Authors: Hassaan Ali Qureshi, Danish Hussain, Ali Hassan, Aon Safdar, Anas Bin Aqeel, Muhammad Rafiq, Zohaib Riaz, Farhan Hussain

Abstract: Lane departure and traffic-sign negligence are leading contributors to road accidents, particularly in regions with non-standardized signage and limited annotated data. Existing Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) solutions are often developed as disjointed submodules, are rarely validated for real-time operation, and struggle to balance accuracy with low-latency inference for embedded deployment. We address these gaps with a unified, edge-deployable ADAS framework that simultaneously performs lane-departure warning (LDW) and traffic-sign detection and recognition (TSD/TSR), and validate the proposed system on automotive-class devices. Our framework combines a lightweight, lane-segmentation-driven LDW, which includes a drivable-area fallback for degraded markings, with a two-stage TSD/TSR pipeline consisting of efficient sign localization followed by fine-grained classification, designed to preserve accuracy at embedded latency. To support region-specific deployment under data scarcity, we curate a 35-class local traffic-sign dataset and introduce a generalized augmentation and balancing profile, expanding the corpus from 359 images to 8,750 samples. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, the integrated system sustains 15 FPS end to end (32 FPS for LDW and 18 FPS for TSD/TSR). The TSD/TSR branch achieves 97.4 mAP for detection and 95.6% validation accuracy (93.1% on a local real-world set) while maintaining an approximately 13.9 M parameter footprint. Relative to recent methods that target a single task or report results only on desktop-class GPUs, our approach delivers both LDW and TSD/TSR with real-time performance on edge hardware, providing a practical pathway to low-cost, field-ready ADAS in resource-constrained settings.

new CASE: Complementary Articulation-Aware Speech Encoder to Enhance Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation

Authors: Jaehong Myung, Seungho Eum, Taegon Kim, Hyunjung Chung, Unsang Park

Abstract: General-purpose self-supervised speech encoders provide strong acoustic representations, but their pretraining objectives are not explicitly aligned with the visible articulatory dynamics required by speech-driven 3D facial animation. We propose CASE (Complementary Articulation-aware Speech Encoder), a complementary speech encoder adapted by contrastively aligning short speech clips with continuous 3D lip-mesh VQ-VAE latents. After adaptation, the geometry branch is removed, and the audio-only CASE representation is fused with the baseline SSL speech representation through residual cross-attention, while retaining the motion-decoder architecture and objective. Across four VOCASET baselines, CASE reduces mean lip vertex error by 2.8-6.0%, and mean full-face vertex error decreases in every system. Under the same fusion protocol, CASE yields lower mean LVE than the unadapted AV-SE stream on all four generators, with model-dependent margins. Because adaptation uses Korean speech-geometry pairs and evaluation uses English VOCASET, the result is consistent with cross-language downstream transfer under a shared English-pretrained audio-visual prior.

new MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes

Authors: Yifei Wang, Wei Tian, Wenhua Bao, Jia Zhou, Hanshi Wang, Fudong Ge, Jianhua Wu, Shuai Yuan, Zhipeng Zhang, Xingliang Liu, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Bingzhao Gao

Abstract: Driving-scene reconstruction via feed-forward Gaussian splatting from sparse multi-view images remains challenging due to two factors. First, cross-camera photometric inconsistency, caused by variations in exposure, ISP, and illumination, can be incorrectly absorbed into Gaussian geometry. Second, unreliable local geometric supervision arises from normal-based constraints near depth discontinuities. To address these issues, we present \textbf{MCSplat}, a multi-view consistent feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework for driving scenes. MCSplat constructs a canonical appearance space from depth-guided multi-camera correspondences to decouple geometry learning from camera-specific appearance. A multi-scale Bilateral Grid Transformer restores raw camera appearance from canonical renderings, enabling photometric supervision without contaminating Gaussian geometry. To improve local geometric reliability, we estimate Fisher-information-based uncertainty from photometric sensitivity and use it to adaptively weight surface-oriented self-supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and generalization across driving datasets. Geometry-oriented evaluations further reveal enhanced cross-view depth consistency and local surface-normal agreement, while qualitative results show fewer geometric artifacts and more coherent structures across overlapping views.

new Local Evidence, Global Failure: Diagnosing Speech-Vision Temporal Composition in Audio-Visual Language Models

Authors: Jaehong Myung, Seunghun Oh, Unsang Park

Abstract: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) can fail at full-video speech-vision decisions even when useful visual evidence is locally recoverable. We introduce Temporal Evidence Decomposition (TED), a training-free diagnostic framework that separates local visual verification from speech-relative aggregation. Automatic speech recognition supplies a transcript and utterance interval. TED queries audio-free windows with the transcript for Temporal Alignment and Forecasting, or answer candidates for Cross-Modal Temporal Binding, then aggregates evidence relative to that interval. Across four frozen AV-LLMs on SVHalluc, Temporal Forecasting accuracy rises from 29.3-33.7% under full-video questioning to 79.3-82.2% with TED. Query replacement reduces recovery; the observed anchor remains beneficial when temporal-region availability is held fixed. Physical-isolation and timing-shortcut controls test alternative explanations. The findings distinguish locally recoverable evidence from successful full-video decisions, motivating explicit separation of narration content, utterance timing, and time-indexed visual evidence.

new LateMatch: Breaking the Interaction Bottleneck via Cacheable Matching for Efficient Visual Localization

Authors: Mohammad Omama, Aeyan Ashraf, Sandeep Chinchali

Abstract: Visual localization is critical for embodied agents, but deploying state-of-the-art deep feature matchers on edge devices is fundamentally limited by their massive computational cost. Standard deep matchers tightly interleave intra-image context building and inter-image matching at every layer, creating a severe interaction bottleneck. Localizing a single query against K database images forces the system to execute the full network K independent times with no capacity for caching. To break this bottleneck, we advocate for a paradigm shift toward cacheable image matching. We realize this paradigm with LateMatch, a versatile approach that restructures existing matchers by deferring inter-image interaction to their final layers. By isolating intra-image processing into offline-cacheable Context Blocks, only a small set of Interaction Blocks must be executed online. To further optimize LateMatch, we introduce E-SToRE (Entropy-guided Spatial Token Reduction and Expansion). E-SToRE leverages the decreasing Shannon entropy of the late Interaction Blocks to dynamically reduce token counts just prior to cross-image interaction. Evaluated across HPatches, ScanNet, MegaDepth, ETH-3D, and Aachen, LateMatch reduces effective computational cost by over 2x compared to standard deep matchers, while E-SToRE yields an additional 10% to 14% savings with negligible degradation in accuracy.

new Painting Change Map as guidance for generating painting processes

Authors: Markus Pobitzer, Chang Liu, Niccol\`o Biondi, Nicu Sebe

Abstract: Digital art generation has undergone a massive paradigm shift, moving from static image synthesis to dynamic video generation that can mimic the human painting process. While existing models can synthesize visually stunning time-lapses of paintings being created or "unpainted," they largely treat the creative process as a black box. Current conditioning mechanisms are either too rigid, relying on static geometric cues like Canny edges or depth maps, or too holistic, utilizing simple scalar progress variables that offer no localized control. Consequently, users lack the agency to steer how a painting evolves over time. In this work, we argue that true control over the video generation of artwork requires a joint understanding of two fundamental dimensions: where an artist acts, and when those actions take place. To achieve this, we introduce the Painting Change Map, a novel spatio-temporal control mechanism that explicitly tracks normalized structural changes across a 1,000-timestep continuum, a resolution sufficient to capture fine-grained stroke-level changes while remaining computationally tractable. By mapping localized visual differences into an encoded RGB space, our representation enables fine-grained guidance for both the forward painting and reverse unpainting processes. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates the efficacy of our approach. We outperform existing control baselines and achieve competitive or superior results compared to state-of-the-art painting methods. Furthermore, under oracle conditions, our method surpasses all baselines by a significant margin. Code is available at https://github.com/Markus-Pobitzer/painting-change-map.

URLs: https://github.com/Markus-Pobitzer/painting-change-map.

new Only Means Only: what a harmonization benchmark score averages over

Authors: Imad Bulji\'c, Delaida Muminovi\'c

Abstract: Image harmonization methods adjust the colour and lighting of an object pasted into a photograph so that it looks native to its new scene, and they are ranked by average error on one benchmark whose test images are real photographs with one object recoloured. One photograph can yield several such test images, and the benchmark promises that no photograph appears in both the training and the test split. We find that 1,399 photographs do, and the composites built on them are a quarter of the test set. Duplicate checks over file names or bytes miss this, because every composite is a different file. On that quarter the three methods we score end to end read two to five times lower error than on the rest, but most of the gap is composition rather than the sharing: the shared composites come almost entirely from one of the benchmark's four source collections, and inside that collection the gap falls to about one and a half times. An official score is therefore an average over two populations, mixed in a proportion the benchmark does not report. We release a test list of 5,581 composites whose construction identities do not appear in training, with four confirmed near-duplicate pairs disclosed rather than removed, adoptable without retraining at the price of one rescore per checkpoint. We leave open whether the sharing itself changes what a model learns.

new ATLAS: Attention-Guided Test-Time Latent Selection for Compositional Visual Autoregressive Generation

Authors: Hossein Shahabadi, Raya Namazi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah

Abstract: Visual autoregressive models produce convincing images but can misassign attributes and spatial relations. Searching multiple generation paths can improve composition, yet completing every candidate is costly. We introduce ATLAS, a training-free framework that uses the frozen generator's internal attention to guide search before final images are available. Within-prompt diagnostics identify attention-derived scores that predict final compositional preferences on Infinity, with category-dependent transfer to Switti. ATLAS uses these on-the-fly signals to progressively concentrate computation on promising trajectories. It maintains multiple coarse alternatives, prunes candidates without decoding at intermediate scales, and reserves image-space evaluation for a final choice among partial trajectories. ATLAS scales effectively on both backbones, achieving higher mean scores on the evaluated T2I-CompBench and GenEval categories as more computation is devoted to search. At the largest tested budget, the targeted T2I-CompBench mean improves by over 10% relative to each backbone. Separate profiles show over 50% less generation time than completing and evaluating all candidates at equal initial counts, alongside lower peak allocated GPU memory. Relative time savings are larger at the higher tested candidate count. Together, these results support scalable compositional search: additional sampling expands exploration, while attention-guided selection limits continuation cost without parameter updates or gradient-based optimization.

new A 3D-Driven Framework for Moving-Camera Perspective-to-360{\deg} Video Generation

Authors: Michael Wakeham, Mrinmoy Kumar Das, Wenqi Wang, Ayush Tewari, Boqing Gong, Deepti Ghadiyaram

Abstract: Turning a moving-camera perspective video into a 360{\deg} video requires more than just generating content outside the input frame: observations revealed over time must be preserved, unseen regions completed, and the resulting scene kept consistent as the camera viewpoint changes. Existing methods assign these different requirements to a single conditional video model, requiring them to be jointly learned from panoramic video data. We instead present a modular, 3D-driven framework that distributes these three responsibilities across specialized components, all connected through a shared scene representation. Input observations are reconstructed explicitly in 3D, while a pretrained panoramic image model completes unobserved content from a selected panoramic render. This generated content is lifted into the shared 3D scene, where it remains spatially anchored across camera viewpoints. Without requiring any additional panoramic-video training, our framework achieves state-of-the-art input-view fidelity, perceptual quality, and geometric consistency on a static-scene subset of the Argus evaluation set. These results support our decomposed, 3D-driven formulation as a promising alternative to direct video generation in this setting.

new PolarVis: A Dataset and Diffusion Framework for RGB-to-Polarization Perception in Adverse Driving Scenes

Authors: Ruilin Huang, Jue Wang, Zhen Tian, Xia Hua, F. Richard Yu

Abstract: Reflections, glare, transparent structures, and material-dependent appearance variations can introduce ambiguity into RGB-based visual perception in vehicle-relevant environments. Polarization provides complementary reflection- and material-sensitive information, but its acquisition requires dedicated sensing hardware. This paper presents RGB-P Wild, a real-world dataset containing 10,000 paired RGB and four-angle linear-polarization image sets, together with PolarVis, a diffusion-based framework for recovering polarization representations from a single RGB image. PolarVis combines hierarchical RGB feature extraction, diffusion-based feature refinement, four angle-specific decoders, and multi-scale attention recalibration to reconstruct polarization intensity images at $0^\circ$, $45^\circ$, $90^\circ$, and $135^\circ$. On RGB-P Wild, PolarVis achieves a normalized-domain MSE of 0.0465, a PSNR of 27.83 dB, and an SSIM of 0.8597. Compared with the released PolarAnything model under the adopted evaluation protocol, PolarVis obtains an AoLP error of $25.66^\circ$ and a DoLP MAE of 0.0404, compared with $46.03^\circ$ and 0.1084, respectively. Cross-dataset evaluation on vehicle-mounted imagery further examines transfer beyond the training domain. In downstream evaluation, a frozen PCDNet achieves AP50/AP50:95 of 86.3%/59.1% on 990 RGBP-Car test images using PolarVis-generated polarization, compared with 87.0%/59.8% using measured polarization. These results indicate that RGB-derived polarization retains useful polarimetric information for the evaluated perception tasks, while remaining distinct from calibrated physical polarization measurements.

new RAHF-Net: Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion for LiDAR-Assisted RGB Semantic Segmentation

Authors: R. D. Lin, Pengcheng Weng, Ge Wang, Han Ding, Fei Wang

Abstract: This paper studies LiDAR-assisted RGB semantic segmentation, where LiDAR point-cloud features improve dense pixel-wise predictions in the RGB image plane rather than 3D point labels or detections. Existing 2D fusion methods often project point clouds into shallow depth/range maps and apply spatially uniform fusion, discarding rich 3D structure and ignoring the range-dependent reliability of outdoor LiDAR. We propose RAHF-Net, a Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion Network. Its Cylindrical-to-Perspective (C2P) module projects pretrained cylindrical voxel features into the image plane, preserving structured 3D semantic priors. A Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion (RAHF) module then uses a soft depth-derived range mask to perform LiDAR-guided geometric enhancement in reliable near-field regions and visual-context enhancement in sparse far-field regions. On KITTI-360, RAHF-Net achieves 65.76 mIoU, outperforming representative RGB-only and RGB-LiDAR baselines, including CMX by 1.45 points. Experiments on DELIVER further demonstrate improved robustness under adverse weather, illumination degradation, and sensor corruption.

new MT Forcing: Towards Stable and Consistent Multi-Turn Image Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion

Authors: Houyuan Chen, Fanzhou Wang, Xiangyu Fan, Zesong Qiu, Yukun Wei, Songlin Yang, Zhitao Yang, Lvmin Zhang, Pei Yang, Hao Zhao, Lei Yang, Anyi Rao

Abstract: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, enabling more effective interactive visual content creation for users. However, existing methods often exhibit noticeable drift after only a few editing turns, manifesting in two aspects: 1) unstable visual quality, with accumulating artifacts and degraded details; and 2) inconsistent image content, with unintended changes to preserved regions and prior edits. To address these challenges, we propose MT Forcing, a novel training paradigm for multi-turn image editing with unified multimodal models (UMMs) based on autoregressive diffusion. Specifically, we propose Single-Turn Distribution Matching Distillation (Single-Turn DMD), which supervises student self-rollouts with a teacher that applies cumulative edits to the source image in a single turn, providing visual-quality guidance without recursive error accumulation. Additionally, we introduce Teacher-Forcing Guidance, which supervises history-dependent transitions on reference trajectories during warmup and as a regularizer during distillation, encouraging cross-turn content consistency beyond what per-turn distribution matching alone can ensure. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the multi-turn image editing capabilities of UMMs, yielding more stable visual quality and stronger cross-turn consistency.

new UniState: Unifying Memory and Intervention for Controllable World Simulation

Authors: Jaeseok Jeong, Kyungmook Choi, Sohyun Chung, Youngsik Yun, Youngjung Uh

Abstract: World models offer increasingly rich environments for exploration, yet intervening in a world while observing the consequences from freely chosen viewpoints remains challenging. We tackle these challenges by introducing UniState, a framework for controllable world simulation built on a unified world-state representation. This representation unifies spatial memory and user interventions. Users specify object motion directly within spatial memory, while independently choosing the camera trajectory from which the resulting world state is observed. This unification makes the relationship between the scene and the requested changes explicit, removing ambiguity between object motion and viewpoint change from the control specification. Authors: Shuochen Chang, Bingjie Gao, Qingyang Liu, Qianli Ma, Yibo Miao, Haonan Zhao, Zhaohe Liao, Xiaofeng Zhang, Jiangtong Li, Li Niu

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant scalability challenges in long-video understanding due to quadratic attention complexity and context window constraints. Authors: Eli A. Underwood, I. Taylor McKechnie, Leslie M. Collins

Abstract: Cross-modal alignment of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery to natural language is constrained by two distinct failures. On zero-shot SAR scene classification, our approach outperforms fine-tuned baselines using up to 8x less training data: DFC2020 (+10.3% R@1, +15.5% mAP), EuroSAT-SAR (+15.7% R@1, +12.2% mAP), BigEarthNet-MM (+14.7% R@1). Authors: Zhongfei Qing, Xiaoxiang Zhao, Ling-Hao Chen, Zhongang Cai, Wenjia Wang, Yifan Wu, Qianying Liu, Wei Zeng, Bo Hu, Songnan Li

Abstract: This work explores monocular motion capture for dragon-type characters, which currently relies on manual keyframing due to the lack of high-quality datasets and parametric models. Authors: Benjamin Loison (Agence Minist\'erielle pour l'IA de D\'efense, France, ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France), Quentin Bammey (T\'el\'ecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, LTCI, Palaiseau, France), Thibaud Ehret (Agence Minist\'erielle pour l'IA de D\'efense, France), Rafael Grompone von Gioi (ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France), Pablo Mus\'e (ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France, IIE, Facultad de Ingenier\'ia, Universidad de la Rep\'ublica, Uruguay), Marina Gardella (ENS Paris-Saclay, Universit\'e Paris-Saclay, CNRS, Centre Borelli, Gif-sur-Yvette, France)

Abstract: Photo Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) is widely regarded as the most reliable marker for source camera identification. Recent studies, however, report high correlations between images and fingerprints from different modern smartphones, which calls into question the discriminative power of PRNU on these devices. Authors: Ang Liu, Xiang Gu, Ruikai Li, Qiyue Wang, Yizhe Fan, Hao Shan, Ziyang Yan, Han Jiang, Zhenning Li, Xiaoshuai Hao, Yilong Ren, Zhiyong Cui, Haiyang Yu

Abstract: Multimodal perception improves autonomous-driving performance by combining complementary sensor information. Authors: Wenyi Lian, Zheng Zhao, Thomas B. Sch{\"o}n

Abstract: Test-time scaling of diffusion models with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) has become a promising strategy for sampling under user-specified rewards, such as human preference scores. Code is available at https://github.com/shermanlian/NR-SMC.

URLs: https://github.com/shermanlian/NR-SMC.

Authors: Antonio Scardace, Silvia Ingala, Sebastiano Battiato, Daniele Rav\`i

Abstract: Spatiotemporal forecasting of 3D anatomical changes is a critical generative vision challenge for modeling Alzheimer's Disease (AD) progression. Code is available at: https://github.com/antonioscardace/MC-LDM.

URLs: https://github.com/antonioscardace/MC-LDM.

Authors: Mingcong Ding, Babette B\"uhler, Tim F\"utterer, Ulrich Trautwein, Enkelejda Kasneci

Abstract: Recognizing fine-grained bodily behaviors, such as self-grooming, postural shifts, and backchanneling, is a useful intermediate step for computational social signal analysis. Authors: Xueyang Li, Alec Girten, Peng Zeng, Mingze Jiang, Shaoyang Huang, Gelei Xu, Danny Z. Chen, Yiyu Shi, John N. Kheir

Abstract: Patients admitted to pediatric ICU and cardiac ICU often require intensive perioperative support and frequent chest radiography to monitor support devices, extravascular lung water, and body-wall edema. Radiographic interpretation and analysis is often difficult due to superimposed anatomic and iatrogenic structures that obscure clinically relevant signals. new SlimFormer++: Token Mixing Where It Matters for Efficient 3D Medical Image Segmentation

Authors: Yang Hong, Lei Zhang, Zhihong Liu, Jianqing Mo, Xujiong Ye

Abstract: To determine where computation is needed in volumetric segmentation networks, we analyze block-level redundancy and stage-wise token-mixer contribution. Centered Kernel Alignment reveals high input-output representational similarity within blocks of representative convolutional, hybrid, and Transformer-style segmentation networks. These findings motivate SlimFormer++, which uses Selective Mixing blocks with windowed Mamba mixing in the first encoder stage and only residual channel MLPs in deeper stages. The source code is available at https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlimFormerPlusPlus

URLs: https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlimFormerPlusPlus

Authors: Xiyuan Liang, Yu Wang, Zuhao Yang, Ziting Wang, Duo Li, Sudong Wang, Zhongyu Yang, Xiaoqin Zhang, Ling Shao, Shijian Lu

Abstract: Video large multimodal models have improved at identifying cross-frame visual evidence and conducting open-web retrieval, as reflected in recent video deep research (VDR) benchmarks. However, existing VDR benchmarks primarily evaluate tool-use trajectories and final responses without verifying whether a model actually uses the temporal video information or the retrieved web evidence. To fill this gap, we introduce \method{}, an evidence-grounded benchmark with three features. First, it combines human review with restricted-access probing across multiple models to exclude questions answerable from parametric knowledge or a single information source. Our benchmark is publicly available at \url{https://huggingface.co/datasets/hh721/vdr_temp}.

URLs: https://huggingface.co/datasets/hh721/vdr_temp

new From Seeing to Reporting: A Theory of Reliable Visual Set Generation in Vision-Language Models

Authors: Junzhe Shi, Yuan Gan, Shida Jiang

Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are asked to report what they see: to count objects, box them, parse a screen or pick a click target (GUI grounding). We argue that reporting is part of the visual task, not merely its formatting. In a dense scene with 173 shapes, GPT-6.1 lists 173 records that match every shape, yet the counts it states in the same response sum to 188. From Seeing to Reporting (FSR) is a theory of visual reporting and a set of inference-time procedures that improve the reports of frozen VLMs. It models reporting as a chain from responses to decoded records, constructed sets and task answers, linked by task-compatible matching. The chain gives exact relations for deleting records, averaging their coordinates and switching readouts, and it splits the error of one answer chosen among several calls into missing candidates, lost representatives and wrong choices. These relations guide procedures for counting, detection, document layout, screen parsing and GUI grounding that use the task specification and a shipped configuration, without requiring labels from the target task. On 50 dense synthetic scenes, a one-call reporting-and-decoding protocol cuts per-type count error by 85.2% for GPT-6.1 and 98.8% for Claude Sonnet 5.5. On 600 ScreenSpot-Pro items, a GUI-grounding tier that combines three models lowers the miss rate from 13.67% for GPT-6.1's two-stage zoom to 9.33%, against 12.67% for three such zooms combined by a cluster vote at about the same cost. A plain vote over the same three models misses 12.33%: the other models supply the candidates, and selecting among them turns those candidates into fewer misses. We release the protocols, the stored responses and the analysis code.

Authors: Abteen Arab, Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai

Abstract: We introduce ReDT, a feed-forward visual geometry transformer designed to scale multi-view reconstruction to high-definition (HD) inputs. Existing visual geometry transformers are typically trained at fixed, standard definition (SD) resolutions and exhibit degraded reconstruction quality and poor computational scaling to high input resolutions. While recent efficient architectures reduce the complexity of inter-frame attention, expensive intra-frame and encoder attention remain largely unaddressed, making HD reconstruction impractical with existing architectures. The key idea of ReDT is to first map each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, compute correspondences in this compact constant-size basis space, and then project the outputs back to the original resolution for dense prediction. By decoupling the internal representation from input resolution during attention, ReDT substantially reduces the computational cost of high-resolution 3D reconstruction and improves model performance at all resolutions. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets spanning SD to FHD (2K) show that ReDT outperforms state-of-the-art visual geometry transformers in both reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. For instance, on the ETH3D (2K) dataset, ReDT achieves a $16\times$ speedup, a $34\%$ reduction in peak GPU memory usage, and a $33\%$ reduction in chamfer distance over VGGT-$\Omega$. \href{https://redt.github.io}{Project Website.}

URLs: https://redt.github.io

Authors: Duc Kieu, Kien Do, Minh Khoa Le, Tung Kieu, Dang Nguyen, Thin Nguyen

Abstract: Any-to-any generation seeks a single model that translates flexibly among text, image, and audio, yet existing approaches either require fully aligned multimodal tuples or a shared representation that suppresses modality-specific structure. Authors: Fahad Iqbal, Shayan Mirzabeigi

Abstract: Accurate recognition of construction site elements is essential for the application of deep learning (DL) in the construction industry. Our results demonstrate that transferability is not a detector-only property: the input-generator distribution strongly influences both evasion effectiveness and attacked-image quality. MIG and MuMoDIG exhibit pronounced dependence on the detector--generator pair, whereas Tricker provides more uniform white-box evasion and image quality. URLs: https://github.com/Sundas058/CGPLR.

Authors: Wenqing Wang, Joonghyuk Shin, Jonathan Tremblay, Chan Hee Song, Yun Fu

Authors: Yang Zheng, Zizhang Li, Boyang Deng, Jan Ackermann, Lei Shu, Yinghao Xu, Jiajun Wu, Gordon Wetzstein, Leonidas Guibas

URLs: https://y-zheng18.github.io/FluidGen/

Abstract: Reference-based 3D scene stylization transfers the appearance of a reference image onto a reconstructed 3D scene while preserving scene geometry. Authors: Daoheng Li, Jianjun Qian*, Mengkai Yan, Jian Yang

Authors: Jie Wang, Guang Li, Zhijian Huang, Jinlong Li, Chenxu Dang, Hangjun Ye, Yahong Han, Long Chen

Abstract: Autonomous driving fundamentally demands dense understanding of visual, semantic, and geometric information, yet existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are typically trained with sparse supervision such as language instructions or trajectory signals. Authors: Haowei Zheng, Zhenyu Zhou, Jiawei Chen, Can Wang, Defang Chen

In this paper, we propose optimal linear leaps (LEAP), a specialized method grounded in theoretical and empirical investigations of sampling trajectory geometry. Built upon low-dimensionality and cross-trajectory consistency, LEAP formulates a supervised least-squares optimization problem within the local trajectory subspace, achieving a precise approximation of future states without model evaluations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LEAP outperforms previous methods across diverse modalities, including text-to-image (Stable Diffusion 3.5, FLUX.1-dev) and image-to-3D (TRELLIS.2) generation. Code is available at https://github.com/zju-pi/LEAP.

URLs: https://github.com/zju-pi/LEAP.

Authors: Zixuan Chen, Depeng Wang, Wei Chen, Ke Xu, Ya Guo, Huijia Zhu, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang

Abstract: Video vision-language models (VLMs) have strong semantic understanding, yet remain unreliable at precise temporal grounding. Existing gains from explicitly aligning video frames with absolute time suggest that VLMs may already encode accurate temporal locations internally but lose precision when expressing them as timestamps. Our analysis across four VLMs and two grounding datasets confirms this hypothesis: attention intervals outperform predicted intervals on approximately 66% of valid examples. We term this discrepancy the temporal generation gap. Because precise temporal annotations are expensive, this finding motivates closing the gap to improve temporal grounding using only unlabeled video-query pairs. We propose Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses internal temporal attention as self-supervision for Group Relative Policy Optimization and applies a ground-truth-free criterion to select high-value samples. SAPO consistently improves temporal grounding across multiple datasets and models spanning weak to strong initial grounding ability. Authors: Hongrui Wu, Kaiwen Tuo, Congcong Wang, Gen Li, Shuai Dong, Xinlei Yu, Yuqi Xu, Haowen Hou, Zelin Peng, Jiaqi Wang

Abstract: Deep research agents are increasingly capable of searching the open web and synthesizing evidence, yet they remain poorly suited to controllable report generation in multimodal deep research. This task requires agents to handle interleaved textual and visual inputs, gather multimodal evidence through multi-step web search, and deliver comprehensive illustrated reports under user-specified requirements. Existing systems face two limitations. During reasoning, they often underuse images discovered along the search trajectory; during generation, they tend to produce fixed-form answers with limited control over report granularity, multimodal composition, and evidence grounding. At its core, MIRA-Harness translates user requirements into generation contracts and connects four stages: evidence collection, report submission, feedback-driven revision, and final delivery. Building on this harness, MIRA-Data constructs high-quality multi-hop multimodal research trajectories, and we post-train foundation models to operate within the workflow. Using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MIRA achieves state-of-the-art performance among open agents on 7 representative, established multimodal-search and deep-research-agent benchmarks, while producing user-aligned illustrated reports with traceable textual and visual evidence.

Authors: Feiyang Hong, Yujie Wei, Bo Zhao, Xiu Su, Hongxun Yao, Shuo Yang

Abstract: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA

URLs: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA

new OmniGround: Strengthening Omni-Modal Temporal Grounding via Attention-Consistency Training

Authors: Zixuan Chen, Depeng Wang, Hao Lin, Ke Xu, Ya Guo, Huijia Zhu, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang

Abstract: Omni-modal large language models can jointly understand video, audio, and text, yet they remain weak at temporal grounding, a capability essential for real-world audio-visual applications. To understand this limitation, we look beyond final predictions and examine the model's internal temporal evidence. To close this gap, we propose TACG (Temporal Attention-Consistency Grounding), a post-training method that treats internal attention as a reliable temporal pivot and aligns it with both the model prediction and the ground-truth annotation through attention-consistency training. Authors: Hyeongjin Nam, Taeryung Lee, Daniel Sungho Jung, Kyoung Mu Lee

Abstract: Joint 4D reconstruction of a human and object from a monocular video is essential for understanding how people interact with their environment. While recent methods have made noticeable progress, capturing such human-object interactions remains difficult due to two main challenges. First, a video typically contains composite semantic context spanning multiple interaction phases, making it difficult to track the temporal changes of the interaction in the reconstruction. Second, under human-object occlusion, a single-view observation contains incomplete visual information about the interaction, resulting in geometrically inconsistent reconstructions. To address these challenges, we introduce HORIA, built upon two core designs. First, we decompose the entire input video into temporally grounded and semantically distinct interaction phases with motion-aware captioning, obtaining a specific text description for each phase. Second, conditioned on these text descriptions of the interaction, we propose an interaction-aware re-rendering that compensates for the limited single-view observation. Specifically, we render the initially reconstructed 4D human and object from novel viewpoints and refine the renderings with a text-to-video diffusion prior, which provides auxiliary novel-view supervision beyond single-view cues. As a result, our framework produces temporally coherent and accurate 4D reconstructions under diverse interaction scenarios, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

Authors: Kesav Kumar Jayakumar, Karthigeyan Thilak

Abstract: We set out to reproduce a recent hallucination-mitigation result on the POPE benchmark. The LLaVA-1.5-7B baseline we measured, 82.21 F1 on the adversarial split, sat 1.21 to 8.67 points above the adversarial baselines we planned to compare against (81.00, 79.30, and 73.54). We looked at the evaluation code and found a readout choice that moves F1 on its own. A two-token logit readout decides yes versus no by comparing two vocabulary IDs, 3582 ("yes") and 1217 ("no"). Across 9,000 greedy-decode questions spanning all three splits, neither ID is generated even once. The model emits " Yes" (token 3869) and " No" (token 1939), because SentencePiece prepends a space byte after the prompt suffix "ASSISTANT:". Read with an eight-token lookup that covers the space-prefixed surface forms, LLaVA-1.5-7B scores F1 0.8221, 0.8498, and 0.8713 on the adversarial, popular, and random splits. That 6.13-point adversarial shift exceeds the adversarial gain reported by five of the six papers we surveyed. None of them states its readout, and our reference ran under 4-bit NF4 quantization, so we cannot say how much of any reported gain a matched evaluation would keep. That comparison stays unresolved until readout and precision are matched. On the fixed baseline we run nine inference-time corrections of our own (none beat it) and dissect why the adversarial split resists logit-level intervention. In a 3,000-question probe, wrong predictions draw more image attention than correct ones (Cohen's $d=-0.46$, $p=1.4\times10^{-24}$), the opposite of what grounding-based corrections assume. A four-readout audit across four further VLMs from three tokenizer families confirms the confound is protocol-level, not model-specific: porting the LLaVA-1.5 IDs verbatim drops F1 to 0.00 on the two disjoint-vocabulary models, whereas a tokenizer-derived readout holds between 0.80 and 0.92.

new Curvature as a Baseline: Monocular Pose Measurement of Cylindrical Objects with Dual Colour Stripe Markers

Authors: Jaesung Hong, Dong Won Lee

Abstract: Thin cylindrical objects offer little space for planar markers. We propose a dual-colour-stripe marker that uses the known curvature of an object to improve pose measurement with a single camera. The boundary between two colours provides a long centre line, while dots and printed edges supply features at different depths. We analyse how this depth separation improves the estimation of rotation about the cylinder axis, or roll. For a camera-facing marker at 15 cm, the Cram\'er-Rao lower bound on roll standard deviation is 2.00{\deg}for a flat marker, 0.38{\deg}for a single curved marker and 0.21{\deg}for a wrap-around marker. Monte Carlo roll RMS errors are within about 10% of the corresponding standard-deviation bounds. A first-order relation connects the sagitta of the curved marker to the roll sensitivity provided by a stereo baseline. The analytical and simulation results explain how curvature improves monocular measurement and provide a basis for designing marker geometry.

Authors: Jiaxuan Sun, Biao Wang, Shuai Li

Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, particularly Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has improved video reasoning in multimodal large language models. However, standard video GRPO varies only linguistic trajectories while conditioning every rollout in a group on the same sampled frames, which can produce homogeneous rewards and weaken group-relative learning when the shared visual evidence is insufficient or distracting. We propose \textbf{FrameGRPO}, a simple and effective reinforcement-learning framework that requires neither auxiliary networks nor changes to the model architecture. Specifically, FrameGRPO combines two lightweight components: (1) \textbf{Multi-Frame Rollouts}, which use only uniform temporal subsampling of a single maximal-frame decode to construct aligned views that diversify visual evidence and reasoning trajectories; and (2) \textbf{Gated Temporal Efficiency Credit}, which selectively reinforces a correct lower-ratio trajectory when all rollouts in a fixed full-ratio reference subset fail, without imposing an unconditional preference for fewer frames. Extensive experiments across diverse video understanding and reasoning benchmarks demonstrate robust overall improvements over standard GRPO, highlighting temporal-view diversification as an effective mechanism for exploration and credit assignment in video MLLMs.

Authors: Shuaiqi Cheng, Jiahao Zhang, Boyuan Gu, Yuxi Chen, Haiying Xu, Zexin Lu, Huiyu Zhou, Xuming Hu

Abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) deliver high-fidelity image and video generation, but inference requires many sequential model evaluations. We link this gap to a mismatch between pointwise distillation and short-horizon execution: a student trained at teacher states need not remain reliable when its own predictions are chained. We propose \textbf{TamedFlow}, which trains a compressed DiT for this deployed role through cross-architecture feature alignment, a near-identity Velocity Alignment Head, and randomized rollout supervision. Authors: Xinyuan Zhao

Abstract: Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind.
